cases.customer_question: What qualification-related obligations changed under the July 2024 Bluetooth SIG registration-process update?
cases.actual_issue: Customers wanted to know whether the July 2024 registration-process update changed qualification requirements, testing expectations, or registration costs.
cases.plain_english_explanation: A process update can sometimes introduce new testing or qualification requirements. In this case, the discussion focused on whether the registration-system changes altered the underlying qualification rules. The answer was that the major impact was procedural rather than a broad increase in testing requirements.
cases.consultant_answer: The consultant explained that the observed changes primarily involved registration categories and process structure. Component and Subsystem treatment was updated, the prior three-year limitation was removed for the affected category structure, and declaration registration became integrated into design registration with a compliance-folder retention obligation. The discussion concluded that there was no general change to Bluetooth test requirements or qualification-fee policy solely due to the process update.
cases.decision_logic: Registration-process changes do not automatically imply new testing requirements. Qualification impact must be determined from the specific QPRD changes rather than assumptions based on a new registration portal or workflow.
cases.final_recommendation: Review the applicable QPRD requirements and ensure a compliant compliance-folder process exists when using the updated registration workflow.
cases.risk_if_done_wrong: Misunderstanding procedural updates can lead to incorrect qualification planning or failure to maintain required compliance records for audit purposes.
